content:
Sam: Heads-up — customer asked for an on-prem POC in an isolated DC. Main asks: signed bundle transport, delta updates, permitted upgrade cadence, and a cost estimate for offline support. Any blockers?
Mari: quick q — will they allow a jumpbox with outbound to our artifact mirror, or fully air-gapped?
Sam: fully air-gapped. They said jumpbox only for initial staging, then locked down.
Leo: ok. For fully air-gapped we need: signed bundles (SBOM), detached installer tar.gz, and a delta apply mechanism. That implies packaging delta patches rather than full images every time.
Anya: security notes — we require bundle signing (private key on our side), SBOM for customer audit, and a reproducible build hash. They also asked about offline cert rotation.
Carla: legal: need to confirm license activation flow — offline entitlements vs node-count keys. Also SOW should cover hotfix windows and rollback SLA.
Sam: customer expects monthly security patches, but wants minimal bandwidth. They asked if we can do weekly tiny patches instead of monthly large ones.
Mari: technically we can produce deltas using binary diffs for the operator image + patchsets for model weights (quantized layers). But large model deltas still big — weight deltas are model-dependent.
Leo: recommended approach: 1) core runtime + plugins container (small) 2) models as separate signed payloads (chunked) 3) delta metadata + a patch apply tool. That lets customers pull only changed chunks.
Anya: for compliance, we need to provide a checklist: SBOM (CycloneDX), GPG-signed bundle, SHA512 manifest, and instructions for offline verification. Also outline key compromise rotation: offline KMS/HSM guidance.
ops-bot: artifact-build:release_2026.03.12-rc4 created — size: 1.2GB (runtime), model_v2.quant: 3.8GB (chunked) — signatures available at /artifacts/signed/1715
Sam: price question — how much to charge for maintaining their offline mirror + signing service + expedited hotfix? PM wants an SKU.
Carla: recommended: 1) base license 2) offline-support add-on (monthly) 3) emergency patch SLA (per-day rate) 4) signed-bundle custody option (we hold keys) or customer holds keys (higher price if we hold keys).
Leo: ops cost ballpark: initial offline pack prep ~ 8 engineer-hours (packaging + SBOM + runbook), recurring monthly ~ 4-6 hrs for delta generation + QA. If we hold signing keys, add ~2 hrs/week ops.
Mari: rollbacks — implement atomic apply with versioned manifests and a safe rollback hook. Keep at least N previous payloads (configurable).
Anya: important constraint: if customer prohibits outbound egress entirely, we must deliver on portable media and provide a tamper-evident signing process. That extends delivery time and legal checks.
Sam: timeline note — customer wants POC in 6 weeks. Feasible?
Leo: feasible if we scope POC to runtime + small sample model (no full model weight sync). Delivery plan: week1 packaging + SBOM, week2 offline installer + runbook, week3 customer staging (media transfer), week4 validation, week5 small delta flow test, week6 wrap + SOW draft.
Carla: will need legal approvals for media transfer clause and acceptance criteria. Also IP export controls if models are large or include third-party weights.
Mari: quick sample rsync command we could give their jumpbox for staged copies:

```
rsync -avP --partial --inplace --checksum /local/artifacts/ jumpbox:/staging/artifacts/
```

Mari: and a sample verification step:

```
shasum -a 512 -c bundle-manifest.sha512
gpg --verify bundle.sig bundle.tar.gz
```

Sam: they asked about upgrade cadence — can we support customer-driven monthly windows, but we should recommend quarterly for full model refreshes.
Leo: yes. Support policy: minor security deltas monthly, model re-trains/weight refresh quarterly. Major version upgrades (runtime) scheduled with 60-day notice.
Anya: also call out fallback policies — if a delta fails in their environment, operator can run `apply --rollback-to X` without contacting us. We'll provide the tool and docs.
Carla: contract language to include acceptance tests and rollback remedies. Also add a limit on emergency binary rebuild windows to avoid unlimited ops exposure.
Sam: ok — next steps: Leo/Mari to draft POC tech runbook + sample commands, Anya to draft checklist for SBOM/signing/rotation, Carla to propose SOW clauses and pricing SKUs. I'll consolidate and send to customer.
Leo: I'll push a minimal repo with packaging scripts and chunker by tomorrow.
Mari: I'll draft the runbook and sample artifacts for the jumpbox flow.
Anya: I'll populate the security checklist and attach example CycloneDX JSON and GPG steps.
Carla: I'll sketch SOW items and the two pricing tiers (customer-keys vs vendor-keys).
Sam: perfect — if everyone can drop updates by EOD Thursday we can hit their timeline. :thumbsup:
